translation_en: Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us; Hisham narrated to us; Mamar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: “Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should honor his guest; whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should maintain ties of kinship; and whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or remain silent.”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Jafar ibn Awn narrated to us; Abu al-Umays narrated to us, from Awn ibn Abi Juhayfah, from his father, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, established brotherhood between Salman and Abu al-Darda. Salman visited Abu al-Darda and saw Umm al-Darda dressed plainly. He asked her: “What is the matter with you?” She said: “Your brother Abu al-Darda has no interest in worldly matters.” Abu al-Darda came and prepared food for him, then said: “Eat, for I am fasting.” Salman said: “I will not eat until you eat.” So he ate. When night came, Abu al-Darda got up to pray, but Salman said: “Sleep.” He slept, then tried to get up again, and Salman again said: “Sleep.” At the end of the night Salman said: “Now get up.” They prayed, and Salman said to him: “Your Lord has a right over you, your self has a right over you, and your family has a right over you. Give each one its due.” He went to the Prophet and told him about it. The Prophet said: “Salman has spoken the truth.” Abu Juhayfah was Wahb al-Suwa'i; he was also called Wahb al-Khayr.

Abu al-Yaman informed us; Shuayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Abu Bakr ibn Abd al-Rahman informed me that Marwan ibn al-Hakam told him that Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Aswad ibn Abd Yaghuth told him that Ubayy ibn Kab told him that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Some poetry contains wisdom.”

Ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ibn Mahdi narrated to us; Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik. Abu Salamah narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “The truest words a poet has spoken are the words of Labid: ‘Indeed, everything apart from Allah is false.’” Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt nearly accepted Islam.

Yahya ibn Yusuf narrated to me; Abu Bakr informed us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurairah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, said: “Wretched is the servant of the dinar, the dirham, the fine cloak, and the striped garment. If he is given, he is pleased; if he is not given, he is displeased.”

Abu Asim narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata, who said: I heard Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If the son of Adam had two valleys of wealth, he would seek a third. Nothing fills the son of Adam's belly except dust, and Allah accepts the repentance of whoever repents.”

Muhammad narrated to me; Makhlad informed us; Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I heard Ata say: I heard Ibn Abbas say: I heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If the son of Adam had a valley of wealth, he would love to have another like it. Nothing fills the son of Adam's eyes except dust, and Allah accepts the repentance of whoever repents.” Ibn Abbas said: I do not know whether this is from the Quran or not. He said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr say it from the pulpit.

Musaddad narrated to us; Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik, from Abdullah ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal, from al-Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said to the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: “Did you benefit Abu Talib in any way?”

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us; Ibn Abi Adi narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say something similar.

Muhammad ibn Abdullah narrated to me; Muhammad ibn Sabiq narrated to us; Zaidah narrated to us; Hisham ibn Urwah narrated to us, from his father, who heard al-Mughirah ibn Shubah relate from Umar that he consulted them about a woman who miscarried, like the preceding report.

Said ibn al-Rabi narrated to us; Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abd Rabbih ibn Said, who said: I heard Abu Salamah say: I used to have dreams that made me ill, until I heard Abu Qatadah say: I too used to have dreams that made me ill, until I heard the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “A good dream is from Allah. If one of you sees something he likes, let him tell only someone he loves. If he sees something he dislikes, let him seek refuge in Allah from its evil and from Satan's evil, spit lightly three times, and tell no one about it, for it will not harm him.”

Ibrahim ibn Hamzah narrated to us; Ibn Abi Hazim and al-Darawardi narrated to me, from Yazid, from Abdullah ibn Khabbab, from Abu Said al-Khudri, who heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, say: “If one of you sees a dream he likes, it is from Allah, so let him praise Allah for it and tell it to others. If he sees something else that he dislikes, it is from Satan; let him seek refuge from its evil and tell no one about it, for it will not harm him.”

Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to me; al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from Ubaydullah ibn Abdullah ibn Utbah, that Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, used to relate that a man came to the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, and said: “Last night I saw in a dream a canopy dripping with butter and honey. I saw people reaching up to take from it, some taking much and some little. Then there was a rope extending from the earth to the sky. I saw you take hold of it and rise. Then another man took hold of it and rose with it, then another man took hold of it and rose, then another man took hold of it and it broke; then it was joined again.” Abu Bakr said: “Messenger of Allah, may my father be sacrificed for you, please let me interpret it.” The Prophet said: “Interpret it.” He said: “The canopy is Islam. What dripped of honey and butter is the sweetness of the Quran, from which people take much or little. The rope extending from heaven to earth is the truth you follow: you take hold of it, and Allah raises you by it. Then a man after you takes hold of it and is raised by it; then another man takes hold of it and is raised by it; then another man takes hold of it, but it breaks for him, then it is joined for him and he is raised by it. Tell me, Messenger of Allah, may my father be sacrificed for you: was I right or wrong?” The Prophet said: “You were right in some parts and wrong in some parts.” He said: “By Allah, you must tell me where I was wrong.” He said: “Do not insist by oath.”
